newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canalsatellite sets summer TV offer.
newsitem.headline: Canalsatellite sets summer TV offer.

text.p: Canalsatellite, a unit of French pay television group Canal Plus, said on Tuesday it was offering free summer viewing to new subscribers to its digital service.
It said in a statement that anyone subscribing as of now would only pay from September 1.
A Canalsatellite spokeswoman said the idea was to persuade people to sign up before going away on holiday rather than delaying their decision to subscribe.
She said Canalsatellite had done similar summer promotions for its analogue satellite service in the past.
Canalsatellite launched its digital service in April 1996, but its rivals, TF1's Television par Satellite (TPS) and AB Productions ABSat, only launched last winter.

The race for digital subscribers in France is largely between Canalsatellite and TPS. Canalsatellite has said it aims to have 500,000 subscribers by the end of this year, while TPS is aiming to have 300,000 by then.
Canalsatellite had 384,000 subscribers to its digital service as of June 13, the spokeswoman said.
Cable television company Lyonnaise Cable, a unit of Lyonnaise des Eaux, launched a digital cable TV service at the beginning of June. Its decoder can receive both Canalsatellite and TPS.
